name.text: Determining general fertility and total fertility rate for women

questiontext.text:
From the figures given below calculate the female gross reproduction rate if the ratio of male and female children is \({@male_ratio@}:{@female_ratio@}\)

Age Group Number of children born to {@total_women@} women
\({@lower_age_groups[1]@}-{@upper_age_groups[1]@}\) \({@count_1@}\)
\({@lower_age_groups[2]@}-{@upper_age_groups[2]@}\) \({@count_2@}\)
\({@lower_age_groups[3]@}-{@upper_age_groups[3]@}\) \({@count_3@}\)
\({@lower_age_groups[4]@}-{@upper_age_groups[4]@}\) \({@count_4@}\)
\({@lower_age_groups[5]@}-{@upper_age_groups[5]@}\) \({@count_5@}\)
\({@lower_age_groups[6]@}-{@upper_age_groups[6]@}\) \({@count_6@}\)
\({@lower_age_groups[7]@}-{@upper_age_groups[7]@}\) \({@count_7@}\)
\(\sum\) \({@total_children@}\)

Note: It is assumed that the number of children born (given) are the total children born during the time {@total_women@} women passed through the age group, i.e in years)

Note: Give your answer correct to \(4\) decimal places

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Calculation of Gross Reproduction Rate \(\textbf{(GRR)}\)

From the figures given below we calculate the female gross reproduction rate given the ratio of male and female children as \({@male_ratio@}:{@female_ratio@}\)

Age Group Number of children born to {@total_women@} women Number of female children born
\({@lower_age_groups[1]@}-{@upper_age_groups[1]@}\) \({@count_1@}\) \(\displaystyle \frac{{@count_1@}\times {@female_ratio@}}{100}={@female_children_count[1]@}\)
\({@lower_age_groups[2]@}-{@upper_age_groups[2]@}\) \({@count_2@}\) \(\displaystyle \frac{{@count_2@}\times {@female_ratio@}}{100}={@female_children_count[2]@}\)
\({@lower_age_groups[3]@}-{@upper_age_groups[3]@}\) \({@count_3@}\) \(\displaystyle \frac{{@count_3@}\times {@female_ratio@}}{100}={@female_children_count[3]@}\)
\({@lower_age_groups[4]@}-{@upper_age_groups[4]@}\) \({@count_4@}\) \(\displaystyle \frac{{@count_4@}\times {@female_ratio@}}{100}={@female_children_count[4]@}\)
\({@lower_age_groups[5]@}-{@upper_age_groups[5]@}\) \({@count_5@}\) \(\displaystyle \frac{{@count_5@}\times {@female_ratio@}}{100}={@female_children_count[5]@}\)
\({@lower_age_groups[6]@}-{@upper_age_groups[6]@}\) \({@count_6@}\) \(\displaystyle \frac{{@count_6@}\times {@female_ratio@}}{100}={@female_children_count[6]@}\)
\({@lower_age_groups[7]@}-{@upper_age_groups[7]@}\) \({@count_7@}\) \(\displaystyle \frac{{@count_7@}\times {@female_ratio@}}{100}={@female_children_count[7]@}\)
\(\sum\) \({@total_children@}\) \({@total_female_children_count@}\)


Finding the Gross Reproduction Rate \(\textbf{(GRR)}\)

\(\textbf{GRR}=\displaystyle \frac{\text{Total births to}\, {@total_women@} \, \text{Women}}{{@total_women@}}=\frac{{@total_female_children_count@}}{{@total_women@}} \approx {@grr@} \)

Note: It is assumed that the number of children born (given) are the total children born during the time {@total_women@} women passed through the age group, i.e in years)
